# happybabytracker UI screenshots (legacy, before the redesign)

> **Frozen.** These are the first-pass design's screenshots, kept unchanged as the "before" half of [Before and after](../wiki/Before-and-after.md). The generator now writes the redesigned screens to `docs/screenshots`; the "Regenerate" section below describes how this set was made and no longer applies to this folder.

<!-- Generated by ui/e2e/screenshots/index.ts: edit the shots or notes.ts, then regenerate. -->

209 screens and states, each at two viewports: **mobile** 390×844 and **desktop** 1280×800,
light colour scheme, JavaScript on, device scale factor 1, full-page captures.
**Initial design:** these screens show the current first-pass design, captured as a baseline for review and later redesign; they are not a final design.
Every value shown is fake stub data from `ui/e2e/stub-api.ts`; no real person or child appears.

## Regenerate

```sh
cd ui
PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome-headless-shell pnpm screenshots
node e2e/screenshots/index.ts --check   # the README lists exactly the PNGs on disk
```

`pnpm screenshots` builds the UI, starts it and the stub API on ports 4173 and 4181 (one Playwright
run at a time), runs `ui/e2e/screenshots/*.shot.ts` (never part of `pnpm test:e2e`), then runs
`index.ts`, which checks that every shot exists in both viewports and nothing else is on disk,
optimises the PNGs with `oxipng` when it is installed (lossless), and rewrites this README.
A shot that is renamed or removed leaves its old PNGs behind: delete them, or the check fails.

## Determinism

The stub API and the UI server run with `ui/e2e/screenshots/freeze-clock.ts` preloaded, and the
browser uses Playwright's `page.clock.setFixedTime`: all three read **2026-11-24T10:30:00Z**
(browser time zone UTC, locale en-US). Ages, dates, "today" and every relative time are therefore
the same on every run. Animations are disabled, reduced motion is emulated, the caret is hidden,
focus is cleared and the pointer is parked before each capture, after the network is idle and the
fonts are loaded. Two consecutive runs produce byte-identical PNGs.

## Fixtures

All from `ui/e2e/stub-api.ts` (passwords are the stub's fake ones), as they stand on 2026-11-24:

| User | Role and kids |
|---|---|
| `admin` | the admin: only `/admin/parents` |
| `ana` (Ana) | guardian of Mia and Ivy (and of Noa, Uma, Oli and a long-named kid the shots add), caregiver of Leo; of Sami in one milestone shot |
| `cleo` (Cleo) | guardian of Leo, Nell, Otto, Pia, Remy and Sami |
| `dan` (Dan) | no kids |
| `bo` (Bo) | invited, no password yet (the invite link) |
| `dee` (Dee) | disabled |

| Kid | Born | Age on the frozen day | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mia | 2026-07-08 | 4 months | UTC |
| Leo | 2024-08-20 | 2 years 3 months | born at 35 weeks 2 days, Europe/Madrid, growth rows from the stub |
| Ivy | 2025-10-24 | 13 months | UTC |
| Nell | 2026-02-24 | 9 months | milestones |
| Otto | 2021-12-24 | 4 years 11 months | milestones on, one retired milestone row |
| Pia | 2021-11-24 | 5th birthday | milestones on |
| Remy | 2026-08-24 | 3 months | born at 32 weeks |
| Sami | 2024-05-24 | 30 months | milestones off (the default past 24 months) |
| Noa, Uma, Oli, NNN… | added by the shots | 10 days; 14 days at 30 weeks; 7 years; 40 days | created through the stub API |

Entries, measurements, doses and courses are seeded per test through the stub API (`seed.ts`);
every test starts from `/__reset`.

## Not captured

- **export-pdf**: the PDF is streamed as a download by `POST /kids/[kid]/export/pdf`; it is not a page.
- Endpoints that are not pages: `/healthz`, `/healthz/api`, `/healthz/reminders`, `/account/notifications/subscribe`, `/logout` (a POST that lands on the sign-in page, `auth/01`).
- The generic “Something went wrong” error page: the stub has no scenario that makes the UI answer a 5xx other than 503.
- The `down` and `slow` API scenarios: they render the same 503 page as `unavailable` (`errors/04`).
- The browser’s own notification permission prompt and a real push subscription: the headless browser cannot subscribe; “This device” is shown by registering a device through the stub and setting its device cookie.
- The “browser cannot receive notifications” message: it needs a browser without Web Push.
- Install / PWA prompts: the app shows no install UI of its own.
- Caps that need hundreds of rows (the 21st medication course, the 501st vaccination): the same field-message pattern as the errors shown.
- Deleting a kid, an entry, a course or a dose: each lands on a page already shown; the confirm steps are captured.
- JavaScript off and dark mode: out of scope by decision.
